newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Eurobourses retreat with the Dow, dlr slips.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Eurobourses retreat with the Dow, dlr slips.

text.p: European shares, which had been trading mixed all day, turned weaker on Monday afternoon after Wall Street opened lower and in quiet currency markets the dollar slipped below 1.67 marks and 122 yen.

London shares were at the day's lows, down almost half a percentage point, influenced not only by the weaker start in New York but also by a batch of heavyweight stocks going ex-dividend, including Barclays and Lloyds TSB .

Investors were also concerned that the strength of sterling -- at its highest level since it left the European exchange rate mechanism in 1992 -- would affect earnings as the corporate results season gets fully under way.

In Frankfurt, German shares, which had earlier ended floor trading flat, fell sharply, more than one percent, in post bourse electronic trade. Dealers said sentiment was still weighed on by the softening of the dollar -- which is negative for German exports.
German shares were likely to remain rangebound in the near future, contaminated by uncertainty about the next likely direction of global markets and the outlook for the dollar, they said.
The 30-share IBIS DAX index was down some 30 points in mid-afternoon, around ten points below the close of floor trading.
In Paris, too, shares which had found some buying support and showed gains in early trading, turned down in the afternoon to trade flat, with sentiment affected by events in New York.
Traders said the market was supported by buying on the first account day although it was trading under the sway of softer domestic and German bonds and the retracement of the dollar.
One focus of the Paris bourse was resorts company Club Mediterranee. Its shares jumped almost 20 percent as investors welcomed the appointment of the head of Euro Disney to the ailing group.

Club Med announced last Friday it was replacing its chairman Serge Trigano with Philippe Bourguignon, head of Disneyland Paris theme park, and surprised the market with a net loss for the 1995/96 year of 743 million francs ($131.3 million).

Analysts said both equities and currency markets were treading water to an extent ahead of U.S. Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan's semi-annual commentary on the U.S. economy to Senate and House committees on Wednesday and Thursday.
His utterances will, as usual, be scrutinized for clues to future U.S. credit policy.
On currency markets, the dollar softened in the European afternoon below the 1.67 mark and the 122 yen level.
The dollar was weakened by perceptions that Germany's economy was perhaps not as ailing as feared and by worries about Japanese firms' fund repatriation.

Concern that Japanese companies might sell more dollars than in usual years to repatriate their funds was sparked by news that Mitsubishi Heavy Industries was planning to liquidate all its dollar-denominated deposits, currently at around $700 million, and convert them into yen.

"The (Mitsubishi) report has set some people in the market thinking that perhaps there's a repatriation story starting here. Certainly this may set off one or two more rumours," said Stewart Newnham, economist at First Chicago here.
Also, dealers said, they shunned taking up aggressive dollar positions ahead of Greenspan's testimony, which is likely to provide the next direction for the U.S. currency.

"We tend to think Mr. Greenspan will raise again some fears about the labour market and the potential for inflation. If he does, the market is going to start factoring in an early rate hike and this should push the dollar to the 1.70 level (to the mark)," said Thomas Rayner, international economist at Societe Generale Strauss Turnbull.

Another factor weighing on the dollar was a Washington Post article on Sunday which quoted sources as saying some senior U.S. officials expressed concern about the U.S. stock market, saying "the higher the market goes, the closer it could be to a correction".
Analysts said this report was causing worries, particularly ahead of Greenspan.
CURRENCIES AT 1515 GMT
The dollar was quoted at 1.6698 marks and 121.95 yen, compared with 1.6883 and 123.20 in late European trade on Friday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1515 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index was down 15.0 points at 4,321.0.
PARIS - The CAC-40 was up 2.72 points at 2,565.56.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index closed up 0.12 points at 3,184.21. The IBIS Bax electronic index was down 27.58 at 3176.21
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold fixed in the afternoon at $353.05, compared with $353.75 at the London close on Friday. ($ = 5.659 French Francs)
